extracted.intended_audience: mathematics instructors and students (those designing or taking courses that include mathematical writing and presentations)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of resources and topic-based guidance for engaging students in writing and speaking about mathematics, intended to help instructors design assignments, give feedback, and teach communication skills in mathematics courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing as Mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and guidance for students writing mathematics in the voice and conventions of the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site collects resources aimed at engaging students in writing about mathematics, whether for learning math or learning to communicate as mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving Effective Math Presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practices for delivering clear, effective oral presentations of mathematical material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples of good math presentations, practice presentations, discussion questions for presentation workshops, and cautions about sample presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talking about Math to Better Understand It
rubrics_metrics.description: Using spoken communication (discussion, explanation) as a learning tool to deepen mathematical understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes presenting to learn and using communication activities to help students internalize concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing about Math to Better Understand it
rubrics_metrics.description: Using writing activities to help students develop and clarify their mathematical understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'writing to learn' approaches and assignments intended to improve conceptual grasp through composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating Effectively with Math Project Teammates
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices and expectations for team communication in collaborative mathematical projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance intended for improving teamwork communication and project coordination among students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions for your Class
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief summary of suggestions instructors should consider when designing a mathematics class that includes communication components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level curricular suggestions; links to more detailed resources across the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailoring mathematical exposition (writing or oral) to the intended audience's background, expectations, and needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core topic; includes resources and considerations for adapting content and level of formality based on audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focusing and structuring longer communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for organizing long papers or talks so that they remain focused and coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers planning the term, term papers, and strategies for guiding the audience through extended content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding the audience through the content
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordering and signposting material so readers or listeners can follow the logical development of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Ordering information so content flows logically' and strategies for information order and connectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering information so content flows logically
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific emphasis on sequencing ideas to create a logical narrative or argument in exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes flow and connectivity as central to clarity; warns against excessive connectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive connectivity: too much of a good thing
rubrics_metrics.description: An anti-pattern warning that over-linking or over-explaining connections can harm clarity or overwhelm the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls attention to balancing connections and not overloading exposition with unnecessary cross-links or digressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing conceptual with formal
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding an appropriate mix between informal conceptual explanations and formal mathematical statements/proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages instructors and students to choose the right balance depending on audience and pedagogical goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining mathematical correctness and sufficient detail while communicating; ensuring definitions, statements, and arguments are precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core principle; pertains to both written and oral mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizing proofs clearly, including the logical flow, use of lemmas, and overall structure of arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance like 'Proof writing; guiding text', 'Order of quantifiers', and 'Types of proof & proof-writing strategies'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of quantifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness of the importance and readability implications of quantifier order in statements and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlighted as a specific technical point in proof-writing and exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof Elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: Striving for proofs that are not only correct but also clear, insightful, and aesthetically pleasing when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a distinct characteristic to aim for in student proofs and mathematical exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of proof & proof-writing strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding different proof techniques and choosing strategies appropriate to the theorem and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers strategy selection and instructional approaches to teaching various proof methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Employing diagrams, figures, and other visuals effectively to support mathematical explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes resources on visuals and 'Latex labels on figures' for production-quality visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wording and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing precise language and correct punctuation to improve clarity and readability of mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among technical exposition topics; relates to standard stylistic conventions in math writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting and using consistent, conventional, and reader-friendly notation in exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses translating concepts into math language and notation choices to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX / Advanced LaTeX Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance on typesetting mathematics and advanced LaTeX usage for producing professional documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Advanced LaTeX Topics' and front-end tools like LyX; also mentions 'Latex labels on figures'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using sources
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cite, incorporate, and acknowledge sources in mathematical writing appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers proper attribution and integrating references into exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment / Feedback and assessment for writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practical methods for evaluating student mathematical communication (writing and presentations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the question 'How can I objectively grade something as subjective as communication?' plus handouts and rubrics ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: How can I objectively grade something as subjective as communication?
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-guidance about creating objective or transparent assessment criteria for communication tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poses strategies and resources for rubric construction and fair grading of writing/presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of effective student talks and papers
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of observable traits that indicate strong student mathematical talks and written papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a focused topic; intended to guide instruction, feedback, and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer critique (on writing and presentations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using structured peer feedback as a tool for improving mathematical communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes resources on peer critique, incremental drafts, and integrating peer feedback into revision cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes and strategies for students to revise drafts to improve clarity, correctness, and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages iterative drafting and provides revision-focused assignment designs and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing to learn
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments and practices that use writing as an instrument for learning mathematical concepts, not just for assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes low-stakes writing and reflective tasks that promote understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting to learn
rubrics_metrics.description: Using presentation activities as a method for students to consolidate and demonstrate learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practice presentations and guidance for structuring presentations as learning experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice presentations / Sample presentations: examples & cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing students with model talks and practice opportunities, along with cautions about common pitfalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes workshops, sample presentations, and discussion prompts for improving delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques to involve listeners, maintain attention, and make mathematical talks accessible and compelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of presentation resources and practice activities aimed at increasing interactivity and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening to mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching students how to be effective listeners of mathematical exposition as a complement to speaking and writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes classroom strategies for developing listening skills and using listening as part of assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative writing and presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Addressing communication tasks that involve numerical, statistical, or quantitative reasoning and how to present them clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets audiences and assignments where quantitative literacy is central to the exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of differing genres of mathematical writing (e.g., expository papers, proofs, reports, reflective pieces) and their conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps instructors design genre-appropriate assignments and assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: English learners & global English
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations and resources for supporting non-native English speakers in mathematical communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses language-access issues and inclusive practices in teaching writing and presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for publishing and writing prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about venues, awards, and publication opportunities for student mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists external opportunities (e.g., MAA Writing Awards) to motivate and recognize high-quality student work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using communication to help reduce math anxiety
rubrics_metrics.description: Employing communication-focused activities to lower affective barriers and build confidence in mathematics students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links pedagogical goals of communication to affective outcomes like anxiety reduction.
